subject: BrightPath: Priority outage — latency & 5xx surge
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@brightpath.health>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-17T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Platform latency & 5xx spike — urgent

Naomi / Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in end-to-end latency and a correlated rise in 5xx errors across our checkout flows around 07:50 PDT. TPS dropped from our baseline ~420 TPS to ~210 TPS and user-facing errors spiked to ~3.8%. Attached is a short CSV of the metrics and a screenshot of the error pattern.

Immediate ask: can your team open a command channel now? Our execs are asking for a timeline — this is impacting a live campaign and will go to the board if it isn't stabilized in the next 2–3 hours.

Quick context: BrightPath is on Redwood Dedicated. We didn't change traffic routing or model variants on our side.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Engineering, BrightPath Health
elena@brightpath.health

Attachments: error_screenshot.png, latency_metrics_0917.csv

From: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightPath Engineering <eng@brightpath.health>
Date: 2026-09-17T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform latency & 5xx spike — urgent

On Thu, Sep 17, 2026 at 08:20 Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena — thank you for the data. We're mobilizing now.

Quick initial findings from the first 15m of traces:
- Root signal: sudden rise in average sequence length for a subset (~12%) of requests, causing KV cache thrash on a small set of serving workers.
- The thrash coincides with model-variant fallbacks (started at 07:48 PDT) — likely triggered by a transient disk I/O jitter on a node pool.
- Error signature: mostly 502/503 from the runtime retry layer, not application-level decode errors.

Immediate actions we are pushing:
1) Route BP traffic off the implicated worker group to a warm pool (started).
2) Enable quantized variant for the affected model for this customer (safer memory footprint).
3) Temporarily tighten the max allowed sequence length for this customer's route to preserve latency SLOs.

I'll post updated trace snippets in the command channel. If mitigations don't show improvement in 10–15m we'll escalate to autoscale burst + cross-region spill.

—David
David Kim
VP, Serving Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightPath Engineering <eng@brightpath.health>
Date: 2026-09-17T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform latency & 5xx spike — urgent

Update from ops (09:00 PDT):
- Worker group re-routing completed at 08:47 PDT. Initial effect: aggregate TPS recovered to ~315 TPS, error rate down to ~1.6%.
- Quantized variant rollout for BP started at 08:52 PDT (canary -> 60% -> full for their route).
- Sequence length cap applied at 08:55 PDT. We see tail latency 95p reduced by ~40% on the affected routes.

Next steps & owners:
- Kimberly: apply short-term autoscale burst (manual) if TPS demand rises >380 TPS in next 30m.
- David: continue trace harvesting and provide a post-mortem hypothesis by EOD.
- Marissa / Naomi: align customer comms and confirm if exec sync required.

Command channel: Zoom started (link in HS-987654321). We'll maintain running log.

Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Operations — Redwood Inference

We can join an 11:00 PDT sync if helpful — preferable for our COO to be on the call.

Elena
